Game on the sports feed this cycle: Oaks at San Antonio — The Oaks' perfect start ends at four. In Indiana, in front of a building at 90% capacity, the Pacers built a 61-42 halftime lead behind a 34-point second quarter and led 82-62 after three. The Oaks answered with 38 points in the fourth and won the quarter 38-22, but the comeback came up four short, Pacers 104 - Oaks 100. Adash Stanley and Austin Reaves led the way with 19 apiece. Stanley hit 5 of 11 from three, and Reaves had 7 assists and 6 rebounds without a turnover. AJ Dybantsa added 15, Wendell Carter Jr. went 5 for 6 for 10 points and 7 rebounds, and T. Jerome chipped in 10 points and 5 assists. The Oaks fall to 4-1. (the rider lift is real only where a station row says "game day")

Game on the sports feed this cycle: Oaks at San Antonio — After the perfect start ended in Indiana, the Oaks went to Toronto and answered with the most lopsided win in franchise history, Oaks 135 - Raptors 75, in front of a 95% crowd. The Oaks led 39-19 after one, 73-40 at the half and 101-62 after three, and nobody played more than 28 minutes. Austin Reaves led with 20 on 4 of 6 from three, T. Jerome had 19 points, 7 rebounds and 7 assists, and Adash Stanley went 4 for 4 from three for 16 with 7 rebounds and 6 assists. Wendell Carter Jr. owned the glass with 14 points and 15 rebounds, 5 of them offensive. The Oaks shot 57 of 91, 19 of 28 from three, handed out 34 assists and turned it over only twice. The Oaks move to 5-1. (the rider lift is real only where a station row says "game day")

Game on the sports feed this cycle: Oaks at KONO — The Oaks opened their first NBA Cup run at home in front of a sold-out crowd and held off the Oklahoma City Thunder, 101-95, behind Dillon Brooks' biggest scoring night as an Oak. The Oaks led after every quarter but never by much: 35-30 after one, 63-60 at the half and 78-74 after a 15-14 third. Brooks played 39 minutes and scored 22 on 8 of 15, hitting 6 of 9 from three, with 4 rebounds, 5 assists, 2 steals, a block and one turnover. In a game this close, his threes kept Oklahoma City at arm's length. Adash Stanley added 21 and 6 assists and went 6 for 6 at the line, though he turned it over 6 times. Wendell Carter Jr. was nearly perfect, 8 of 9 for 19 points and 13 rebounds, and AJ Dybantsa ground out a 13-point, 10-rebound double-double on a 4 for 15 night. As a team the Oaks went 13 of 13 from the line. The Oaks move to 6-1 and 1-0 in Cup play. (the rider lift is real only where a station row says "game day")

sources.name: Elena Soria Dominguez
sources.quote: The documents show sightlines and path widths. They don't show the woman who sets up her cart at the panadería corner every morning, or the way riders slow down to talk to her even when the platform's crowded. Phase II's about geometry, but what I see is that people are already making this place theirs — the question is whether the design lets them keep doing that or just moves them through faster.

sources.name: Eleanor Rivera
sources.quote: At 7:40 on a weekend morning at 12th Street, the shift is quiet in a different way than a weekday. The crowds aren't there, so you hear the announcements bounce off the tile more. And you notice the regulars — the ones who are always there, not the game-day rush. If riders didn't come, most of the time it's the weather or a holiday or something happening downtown. But I can't speak for Coliseum specifically — I wasn't there, and I don't have that platform's view. What I can tell you is that when a station drops more than the usual weekend pattern, it's rarely one thing. It's usually a rhythm stacking up — something at the station, something on the line, something in that neighborhood. But I'd be guessing if I told you where those riders went.

sources.name: Jerald Jensen
sources.quote: The schedule tells you how many people came through. It doesn't tell you why they left. When the Coliseum empties out like that on a weekend, I see it in the trash cans — fewer cups, fewer wrappers, fewer folks lingering after the last train. The platform records don't catch the quiet. They don't catch the feeling that people aren't just missing a train, they're missing a reason to be there. That's what I see.

sources.name: Evan Lewis
sources.quote: Look, I drive that line past the Coliseum plenty, and you can feel it when something's off before you ever see it in a report. On a weekend, yeah, the whole city thins out a bit — that's just how it goes. But when you pull up to that station and it's quieter than it ought to be, even for a Saturday, you start wondering. It's not about the numbers on a page. It's about the folks who used to be standing there who aren't anymore — the ones who found another way, or who just stopped going where they used to go. The platform records don't tell you about them. They don't tell you about the family that used to catch that train to a game and decided it wasn't worth the hassle this month. That's what I see. That's what stays with me after I clock out. I've been doing this long enough to know that when a stop drops like that, it's never just one reason. But nobody's asking the folks who aren't there anymore why they stopped. That's the part the numbers can't say.

The medical hold at Fruitvale last week may still be in riders' memories, even though it reached the platforms this cycle — Coliseum riders could be avoiding the line altogether.

authorizedTexture: plain-language explanation of a Packet-backed infrastructure or transit condition
comparison of two supplied system facts when their relationship remains framed as analysis unless the Packet supplies causation
a restrained forward warning explicitly conditioned on supplied facts and declared missing evidence
unnamed physical texture at a Packet-backed or generic public site that adds no failure, delay, crowd, damage, or operational fact
textureConditions: every named person, place, route, station, system, agency, office, Project, Initiative, business, and organization must come from the Packet
a timestamp, duration, distance, load, capacity, delay, outage, closure, breakdown, maintenance event, or service change requires a supplied source
a cascade or shared-cause claim requires at least two supplied facts plus a Packet-backed link; otherwise it remains an open hypothesis
technical interpretation must use citizen-facing language and must not print raw engine labels, scores, fields, or decimals as public evidence
